extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patentees, patent agents, patent examiners, and legal practitioners concerned with UK (and Union) patent law (late 19th century)
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory rules and procedural standards from the Patents, Designs, and Trade Marks Acts (1883–1888) and related international convention, governing patentability formalities, procedure, jurisdiction, offences, agent registration, exhibition protection, priority, and related definitions. Intended to guide applicants, practitioners, and officials on compliance and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace for prior disclosure or use within specified periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Any description of the invention, or use therein, in the United Kingdom or the Isle of Man during the respective periods aforesaid shall not invalidate the patent which may be granted for the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects subsequent patent rights despite certain prior public disclosures/uses made within specified statutory periods (a statutory 'grace' or priority-like protection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of application for grant under this section
rubrics_metrics.description: The application for the grant of a patent under this section must be made in the same manner as an ordinary application under this Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special routes (e.g., convention/priority routes) nonetheless require the ordinary formality and procedural steps of a standard UK application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order in Council applicability to foreign states/British Possessions
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of this section shall apply only in the case of those foreign states with respect to which Her Majesty shall from time to time by Order in Council declare them to be applicable, and so long only in the case of each state as the Order in Council shall continue in force with respect to that state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parliamentary/statutory provisions may be extended to specified foreign states or possessions by executive Order in Council, and only for as long as the Order remains in force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller/Order in Council power to apply provisions to British Possessions with variations
rubrics_metrics.description: It shall be lawful for Her Majesty, from time to time, by Order in Council, to apply the provisions of the last preceding Act with such variations or additions, if any, as to Her Majesty in Council may seem fit, to such British Possession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Crown may adapt UK patent provisions to colonial/local contexts by Order in Council, including adding or varying terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: False representation that article is patented — offence and penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who represents that any article sold by him is a patented article, when no patent has been granted for the same, shall be liable for every offence on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding five pounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A person is deemed to represent an article as patented if he sells it with the word 'patent', 'patented', or any words expressing or implying that a patent has been obtained, stamped on or otherwise applied to the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on unauthorized use of royal arms in trade — offence and penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who, without the authority of Her Majesty, or any of the Royal Family, or of any Government department, assumes or uses in connection with any trade, business, calling, or profession the royal arms, or arms so nearly resembling the same as to be calculated to deceive, shall be liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding twenty pounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criminalizes use of royal emblems to imply official sanction; penalty is summary fine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for infringement actions in Scotland
rubrics_metrics.description: In any action for infringement of a patent in Scotland the provisions of this Act with respect to calling in the aid of an assessor shall apply, and the action shall be tried without a jury, unless the Court shall otherwise direct; but otherwise nothing shall affect the jurisdiction and forms of process of the Courts in Scotland in such an action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scottish patent infringement actions are to follow specified procedures (assessors, trial without jury by default) while preserving existing Scottish court jurisdiction and forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary offences under the Act in Scotland — jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: In Scotland any offence under this Act declared to be summary punishable on summary conviction may be prosecuted in the Sheriff Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designates appropriate court for summary prosecution of specified offences in Scotland.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation proceedings in Scotland — form and parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings in Scotland for revocation of a patent shall be in the form of an action of reduction at the instance of the Lord Advocate, or at the instance of a party having interest with his concurrence, which concurrence may be given on just cause shown only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revocation (reduction) requires Crown or interested party (with Lord Advocate concurrence); service of writs and summonses to follow existing forms and practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies in Ireland as if patent extended to Ireland only
rubrics_metrics.description: All parties shall, notwithstanding anything in this Act, have in Ireland their remedies under or in respect of a patent as if the same had been granted to extend to Ireland only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects procedural/relief rights in Ireland by treating patents as if they extended to Ireland alone for remedy purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act does not affect jurisdiction of courts in Scotland, Ireland, Isle of Man
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this Act shall affect the jurisdiction of the Courts in Scotland, Ireland, or the Isle of Man in proceedings for infringement, or in any action or proceeding respecting a patent, design, or trade mark competent to those Courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves pre-existing local jurisdiction and judicial competence despite UK-wide legislation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification of register consequent on foreign court orders
rubrics_metrics.description: If any rectification of a register under this Act is required in pursuance of any proceeding in a Court in Scotland or Ireland, a copy of the order, decree, or other authority for the rectification shall be served on the Comptroller, and he shall rectify the register accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court orders requiring register changes must be served on the Comptroller who must then amend the official register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of Act to Isle of Man and special Isle of Man provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: This Act shall extend to the Isle of Man, and nothing in this Act shall affect the jurisdiction of the Courts in the Isle of Man; the punishment for a misdemeanor in the Isle of Man shall be imprisonment up to two years with or without hard labour and with or without a fine up to one hundred pounds; summary offences may be prosecuted and fines recovered by aggrieved persons in the manner summary convictions are then prosecuted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies territorial application and local penal/procedural consequences in the Isle of Man.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional savings on repeal of enactments
rubrics_metrics.description: The repeal of enactments described in the Third Schedule shall not affect the past operation of those enactments, any patent granted, applications pending, appointments made, compensation granted, orders given, rights accrued, liabilities incurred, or anything done under those enactments before commencement; nor interfere with the institution or prosecution of any civil or criminal proceedings, which may be carried on as if the repealing Act had not been passed; nor take away or abridge any protection or benefit in relation to any such action or proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects vested rights, ongoing actions, and past effects from being disturbed by statutory repeal (standard savings clause).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registers under repealed enactments deemed part of Register of Patents
rubrics_metrics.description: The registers of patents and of proprietors kept under any enactment repealed by this Act shall respectively be deemed parts of the same book as the Register of Patents kept under this Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures continuity and unity of official patent registers following repeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation and amendment of earlier general rules by Board of Trade
rubrics_metrics.description: All general rules made by the Lord Chancellor or any other authority under any enactment repealed by this Act and in force at the commencement may be repealed, altered, or amended by the Board of Trade as if they had been made by the Board under this Act; and, subject as aforesaid, such general rules shall, so far as consistent with and not superseded by this Act, continue in force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board of Trade assumes power to manage and update pre-existing procedural rules, subject to consistency with the new Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crown prerogative over letters patent preserved
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this Act shall take away, abridge, or prejudicially affect the prerogative of the Crown in relation to the granting of any letters patent or to the withholding of a grant thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms that statutory law does not displace the Crown's prerogative powers regarding letters patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: General statutory definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions set for purposes of the Act include: 'Person' includes a body corporate; 'The Court' means (subject to provisions for Scotland, Ireland, and the Isle of Man) Her Majesty's High Court of Justice in England; 'Law officer' means Her Majesty's Attorney-General or Solicitor-General for England; 'The Treasury' means the Commissioners of Her Majesty's Treasury; 'Comptroller' means the Comptroller-General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks; 'Prescribed' means prescribed by schedules or by general rules under the Act; 'British Possession' and 'Legislature' are defined for the Act's purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory terms are given precise meanings to govern jurisdiction, authority, and procedural interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'summary conviction' in application to Ireland
rubrics_metrics.description: In the application of this Act to Ireland 'summary conviction' means a conviction under the Summary Jurisdiction Acts (specified acts for Dublin and elsewhere in Ireland), i.e., the Acts regulating duties of justices of the peace and police for the Dublin Metropolitan Police District and the Petty Sessions (Ireland) Act, 1851, and amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local procedural definitions determine the meaning and consequences of summary proceedings in Ireland.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration under s.5(2) (form may be statutory or otherwise)
rubrics_metrics.description: The declaration in subsection two of section five of the principal Act may be either a statutory declaration under the Statutory Declarations Act, 1885, or not, as may be from time to time prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that the required declaration may be given in prescribed forms, including but not limited to a statutory declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller may allow limited extensions for filing and sealing
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete specification may be accepted within extended times, not exceeding one month and three months respectively after the said nine and twelve months, as the Comptroller may, on payment of the prescribed fee, allow; and where such extension has been allowed an extension of four months after the said fifteen months for sealing the patent may be allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative discretion allows limited fee-bearing extensions for filing the complete specification and for sealing, effectively extending statutory deadlines when fees paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of specifications/drawings of abandoned applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application for a patent has been abandoned, or become void, the specification or specifications and drawings accompanying or left in connection with such application shall not at any time be open to public inspection or be published by the Comptroller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abandoned or void applications retain confidentiality; the Comptroller must not publish their contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lawful to grant patents to several persons jointly
rubrics_metrics.description: It is declared that it has been and is lawful under the principal Act to grant a patent to several persons jointly, some or one of whom only are the true and first inventors or inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint patents are permitted even if not all named patentees are true first inventors (recognizes assignments/joint ownership).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitution of 'date of application' for 'date of protection obtained' in s.103
rubrics_metrics.description: In subsection one of section one hundred and three of the principal Act, the words 'date of the application' shall be substituted for the words 'date of the protection obtained.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies triggering date for certain rights/conditions as the application filing date rather than any earlier date of provisional protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings: complete specification may refer to provisional drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement as to drawings shall not be deemed to be insufficiently complied with by reason only that instead of being accompanied by drawings the complete specification refers to the drawings which accompanied the provisional specification; and no patent heretofore sealed shall be invalid merely because the complete specification was not accompanied by drawings but referred to those which accompanied the provisional specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits the complete specification to rely on drawings originally filed with a provisional specification; protects sealed patents from invalidity for that reason alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection for patents/designs exhibited at international exhibitions — notice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The exhibition of an invention at an industrial or international exhibition certified as such by the Board of Trade shall not prejudice the rights of the inventor or proprietor, subject to the conditions mentioned, one of which is that the exhibitor must, before exhibiting the invention, design, or article or publishing a description of the design, give the Comptroller the prescribed notice of his intention to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exhibition protection (temporary novelty safeguard) is conditional upon prescribed prior notice to the Comptroller and compliance with certification by the Board of Trade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order in Council may extend exhibition protection abroad and relax notice
rubrics_metrics.description: It shall be lawful for Her Majesty, by Order in Council, from time to time to declare that sections relating to protection at exhibitions shall apply to any exhibition mentioned in the Order in like manner as if it were an industrial or international exhibition certified by the Board of Trade, and to provide that the exhibitor shall be relieved from conditions of giving notice to the Comptroller, either absolutely or upon such terms and conditions as Her Majesty in Council may seem fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive power to extend exhibition safeguards to foreign exhibitions and to modify or dispense with the notice requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on calling oneself a 'patent agent' — registration required
rubrics_metrics.description: After the first day of July 1889 a person shall not be entitled to describe himself as a patent agent ... unless he is registered as a patent agent in pursuance of this Act; the Board of Trade shall make general rules for giving effect to this section; persons who prove bona fide prior practice shall be entitled to be registered; knowingly describing oneself as a patent agent in contravention is a summary offence with fine up to twenty pounds; 'patent agent' means exclusively an agent for obtaining patents in the United Kingdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a regulated register of patent agents, allows grandfathering of bona fide practitioners, and penalizes false claims to status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller may refuse or require amendment where application/specification/drawings not prepared/presented in prescribed manner
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Examiner reports that the nature of the invention is not fairly described, or that the application, specification, or drawings have not been prepared in the prescribed manner, or that the title does not sufficiently indicate the subject-matter of the invention, the Comptroller may refuse to accept the application, or require that the application, specification, or drawings be amended before he proceeds with the application; and in the latter case the application shall, if the Comptroller so directs, bear date as from the time when the requirement is complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative examination grounds permitting refusal or conditional acceptance subject to required amendments; compliance can affect the application's effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to appeal Comptroller decisions to the law officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Comptroller refuses to accept an application or requires an amendment, the applicant may appeal from his decision to the law officer; the law officer shall, if required, hear the applicant and the Comptroller, and may make an order determining whether, and subject to what conditions, the application shall be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an internal appeal mechanism to the Attorney-/Solicitor-General (law officer) for contested procedural refusals or amendment requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller to notify applicant when application accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comptroller shall, when an application has been accepted, give notice thereof to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duty to serve formal notice of acceptance to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of later-filed similar-titled applications before sealing of earlier patent
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after an application for a patent has been made, but before the patent thereon has been sealed, another application for a patent is made, accompanied by a specification bearing the same or a similar title, the Comptroller, if he thinks fit, on the request of the second applicant, or of his legal representative, may, within two months of the grant of a patent on the first application either decline to proceed with the second application or allow the surrender of the patent, if any, granted thereon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative mechanism to manage overlapping applications and titles; Comptroller may decline or permit surrender to avoid conflicting grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete specification must not claim a different invention than provisional
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions added make clear that a complete specification which describes or claims an invention other than that described in the provisional specification, and that such other invention forms part of an application made by the opponent in the interval between the filing of the provisional specification and the giving of the complete specification, is a ground (for action/objection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents applicants from changing the invention between provisional and complete specifications to the prejudice of third parties who filed intervening applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section provisions suspended while infringement or revocation proceedings pending
rubrics_metrics.description: The foregoing provisions of this section do not apply so long as any action for infringement or proceeding for revocation of a patent is pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures certain statutory effects are held in abeyance during pending litigation to avoid prejudice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of Trade delegation and evidentiary certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: All things required or authorised to be done by, to, or before the Board of Trade may be done by the President or a secretary or an assistant-secretary; documents purporting to be orders of the Board sealed or signed by authorised officials shall be received in evidence as such orders unless the contrary is shown; a certificate signed by the President that any order made or act done is that of the Board shall be conclusive evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits administrative delegation within Board of Trade and establishes conclusive evidentiary effect of presidential certificate unless disproved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commencement and collective citation of Acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment Acts to be construed as one with the principal Act and may be cited together collectively as the Patents, Designs, and Trade Marks Acts, with specified date of commencement for provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory housekeeping: how to cite and when provisions take effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union/national treatment under International Convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjects or citizens of each contracting state shall, in all other states of the Union, enjoy the advantages that their respective laws grant, or shall hereafter grant, to their own subjects or citizens: they shall have the same protection and legal recourse on any infringement provided they observe the formalities and conditions imposed by the internal legislation of each state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principle of national treatment: foreign applicants receive the same protection as nationals subject to local formalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assimilation of domiciled non-Union subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjects or citizens of states not part of the Union, who are domiciled or have industrial or commercial establishments on the territory of any of the Union states, shall be assimilated to the subjects or citizens of the contracting states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides protection to foreign nationals resident or doing business in Union states on similar footing as nationals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of priority and protection for subsequent registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who has duly registered an application for a patent in one of the contracting states shall enjoy, as regards registration in the other states, a right of priority: subsequent registration in any of the other states before expiry of the periods shall not be invalidated by acts in the interval (e.g., registration, publication of the invention, or the working of it by a third party). The terms of priority shall be six months for patents and three months for designs, models, and trade-marks (with an extra month allowed for countries beyond).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes a concrete priority period (6 months for patents) and protects later filings in other Union states from intervening acts that would otherwise destroy novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importation of patented articles from Union states does not cause forfeiture
rubrics_metrics.description: The introduction by the patentee into the country where the patent has been granted of objects manufactured in any of the states of the Union shall not entail forfeiture; nevertheless the patentee shall remain bound to work (exploit) his patent in conformity with the laws of the country into which he introduces the patented objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits import of patentee-made goods from sister-Union states without losing rights, while requiring conformity with local working requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary protection for articles at official international exhibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The high contracting parties agree to grant temporary protection to patentable inventions for articles appearing at official or officially recognised International Exhibitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International exhibition protection shields novelty for exhibited articles under agreed terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to establish governmental industrial property departments and patent publication offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Each high contracting party agrees to establish a special government department for industrial property, and a central office for communication to the public of patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires States to create administrative infrastructure for patent administration and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation and role of International Office (Bureau International)
rubrics_metrics.description: An international office shall be organised under the name of the Bureau International de l'Union pour la Protection de la Propriété Industrielle; the office's functions shall be determined by agreement between the states of the Union and its expenses defrayed by the contracting governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets up an international administrative body to support the Union's objectives, with functions and funding agreed between members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic revision of the International Convention
rubrics_metrics.description: The Convention shall be submitted to periodical revisions, with a view to introducing improvements to perfect the system of the Union; conferences shall be held successively in each contracting state by delegates of the states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides for scheduled conferences and revisions to update and improve the international framework for industrial property.
